discovery: Theoretical foundations of quantum computation and quantum simulation with trapped ions and neutral atoms in optical lattices

nominees.name: Juan Ignacio Cirac
nominees.affiliation: Max Planck Institute of Quantum Optics, Garching, Germany

nominees.name: Peter Zoller
nominees.affiliation: University of Innsbruck and IQOQI Innsbruck, Austrian Academy of Sciences, Austria

subfield: Atomic, molecular and optical physics / quantum information
motivation: Cirac and Zoller turned quantum computation from an abstract idea into a concrete physical program. Their 1995 proposal of a controlled-NOT gate with laser-cooled trapped ions gave the first realistic blueprint for a quantum processor and directly launched the experimental trapped-ion quantum computing field. Their 1998 proposal, with Jaksch and others, showed that cold bosonic atoms in optical lattices realize the Bose-Hubbard model and undergo a superfluid-Mott insulator transition, founding analog quantum simulation with atoms. Together with work on quantum networks, cold-atom entanglement and lattice gauge-theory simulators, these ideas have been verified in countless laboratories and now underpin ion-trap and neutral-atom quantum processors worldwide. Rarely have theoretical proposals been so precise, so experimentally realistic, and so transformative for a whole field of physics. Following the 2025 prize for superconducting circuits, recognizing the atomic-physics foundations of quantum information would be timely.
